subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Silicon dioxide is an example of a:
questions.explain: Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.

questions.q: A covalent bond is formed when atoms:
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form when non-metal atoms share pairs of electrons.

questions.q: In a fractional distillation column, the temperature is:
options: The same all the way up
Hottest at the bottom and cooler at the top
questions.explain: The column is hottest at the bottom and gets cooler higher up, so fractions condense at different heights.

questions.q: Why can graphite conduct electricity?
options: It has delocalised electrons between layers
Each carbon bonds to four others
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon bonds to three others, leaving delocalised electrons that carry charge.

questions.q: The complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces:
questions.explain: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Poly(ethene) is made from ethene molecules by:
questions.explain: Many ethene (alkene) monomers join in addition polymerisation to form poly(ethene).

questions.q: Why is cracking carried out on some crude oil fractions?
options: Demand for short-chain fractions like petrol is greater than supply
There is too little demand for short-chain hydrocarbons
questions.explain: Cracking matches supply to demand, as there is more demand for short-chain hydrocarbons than the supply from crude oil.

questions.q: Which molecule is an alkene?
questions.explain: C2H4 (ethene) fits CnH2n and contains a C=C double bond, so it is an alkene.

questions.q: Crude oil is separated into fractions by fractional distillation according to differences in:
questions.explain: Fractional distillation separates the hydrocarbons by their different boiling points.

questions.q: In diamond, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to how many other carbons?
questions.explain: Each carbon in diamond forms four strong covalent bonds, giving a rigid giant structure.

questions.q: Which of these substances has the lowest boiling point?
questions.explain: Simple molecular substances like oxygen have only weak intermolecular forces, so very low boiling points.

questions.q: Alkenes are described as unsaturated because they contain:
questions.explain: Alkenes are unsaturated because they contain at least one C=C double bond.

questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points?
questions.explain: Only weak intermolecular forces need to be overcome, not the strong covalent bonds.

questions.q: Which statement about alkanes is correct?
options: They all contain a C=C bond
They are unsaturated and decolourise bromine water
They are saturated and do not decolourise bromine water
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated, with only single bonds, so they do not decolourise bromine water.

questions.q: When do ionic compounds conduct electricity?
options: When molten or dissolved in water
questions.explain: Ions are only free to move and carry charge when the compound is molten or in solution.

questions.q: The change of state directly from solid to gas is called:
questions.explain: Sublimation is the change directly from solid to gas without becoming a liquid.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: They are made of free electrons
Strong electrostatic forces throughout a giant lattice
questions.explain: Strong electrostatic attractions in the giant ionic lattice need lots of energy to break.

questions.q: In which state are particles most closely packed and only able to vibrate in fixed positions?
questions.explain: In a solid, particles are tightly packed in a regular arrangement and only vibrate.

questions.q: In the particle model, what is true of particles in a gas?
options: Far apart and moving quickly in all directions
Touching but able to move past each other
questions.explain: Gas particles are far apart and move randomly at high speed.

questions.q: Cracking of long-chain hydrocarbons usually requires:
options: A high temperature and a catalyst (or steam)
questions.explain: Cracking uses high temperatures with a catalyst, or high temperatures and steam.

questions.q: Ethanol can be made by fermentation of sugars using:
questions.explain: Yeast ferments sugar to produce ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Why is graphite soft and slippery?
options: Layers are held together by weak forces and can slide
questions.explain: Weak forces between graphite's layers let them slide over one another.
